sentences.text: Gregory S. Paul estimated this small dinosaur to be about 1.3 meters long and weigh twenty kilograms.
A unique trait of Helioceratops is that its lower jaw tooth row is only 60% longer than its maximum height.
The lower jaw teeth of Helioceratops have up to nine secondary ridges in front of the main ridge and four behind it.
The lower jaws of Helioceratops bear between ten and eleven teeth.
Fossils of a new ceratopsian were discovered at the Liufangzi site in Jilin province, China, during excavations in 2000 and 2002.
The species Helioceratops brachygnathus was named and described in 2009 by Jin Liyong, Chen Jun, Zan Shuqin, and Pascal Godefroit.
The known fossils include a right lower jaw dentary and a left upper jaw maxilla.
Helioceratops may have shared its habitat with the dinosaur Changchunsaurus.
Helioceratops is classified within Neoceratopsia in a basal position outside the Coronosauria clade.
Helioceratops represents one of the most derived non-Coronosauria neoceratopsians, alongside Auroraceratops and Yamaceratops.
Helioceratops is considered a member of the family Leptoceratopsidae.
Helioceratops lived in Asia during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 125 and 94 million years ago.
Fossils of Helioceratops were found in the Quantou Formation near Liufangzi in Jilin province, China.
The time range for Helioceratops is estimated from 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago.
